gaps.why_now: The roadmap still requires perf baselines and thresholds, so the narrowest honest progress is a manifest-backed survey packet that keeps the current benchmark-command and acceptable-limit posture machine-checked without inventing numbers. Live master now ships that packet, and the dedicated survey now carries approved local-only acceptable limits for both landed rollback gates while still leaving shared CI perf coverage explicitly out of scope.

A dedicated Phase 4 survey gate keeps the current correctness-only posture for the shipped atomic64 and bitmap rollback gates measurable without treating that local survey route as shared CI perf approval. With the shared tests-root summary already naming this shipped local-only survey packet, the next honest same-lane step was to close the remaining bitmap acceptable-limit edge without widening the shared validator-first packet.

The local perf-baseline packet now exact-pins the current atomic64 benchmark-command candidate `zig build phase4-runtime-atomic64-diff --build-file zigux/tests/phase4_build.zig` plus the deterministic threshold replay evidence (`runThresholdReplay(1)` checksum `3626254113632800175` with final counter `130322557735600377`; `runThresholdReplay(4)` checksum `9210681150676220922` with final counter `130322557735600376`) without pretending that shared CI owns the route.

The bounded atomic64 replay command is now approved for local Phase 4 perf review because the dedicated survey packet already exact-pins the same replay route and deterministic evidence, and its acceptable limit stays explicitly local-only rather than implying shared CI perf approval.

The local-only atomic64 acceptable limit is now approved as a median `runThresholdReplay(4)` budget of `8192` nanoseconds across seven monotonic samples, because the dedicated survey can keep that bounded replay budget explicit, the current local probe already measured a much lower median on the attached Zig toolchain, and the change keeps shared CI perf claims explicitly out of scope.

The local perf-baseline packet now exact-pins the current bitmap benchmark-command candidate `zig build phase4-bitmap-diff --build-file zigux/tests/phase4_build.zig` plus the deterministic threshold replay evidence (`runThresholdReplay(1)` checksum `5216946504564592253` with final first-set `0`, final first-zero `109`, final weight `1005`, and final nth-seven `123`; `runThresholdReplay(4)` checksum `7942141539243507472` with the same final first-set, first-zero, weight, and nth-seven packet) without pretending that shared CI owns the route.

The bounded bitmap replay command is now approved for local Phase 4 perf review because the dedicated survey packet already exact-pins the same replay route and deterministic evidence, and the acceptable limit now stays explicitly local-only inside that same survey packet rather than widening into shared CI perf approval.

The local-only bitmap acceptable limit is now approved as a median `runThresholdReplay(4)` budget of `131072` nanoseconds across seven monotonic samples, because the attached Zig toolchain replay measured a median of `79135` nanoseconds with a worst sample of `121289`, the deterministic checksum-backed replay packet stayed stable, and the survey keeps that bound explicit without claiming shared CI perf coverage.

The dedicated survey packet now ships the approved local benchmark commands and approved local-only acceptable limits for both landed rollback gates, so the remaining bounded Phase 4 perf gap is a policy decision owned by the Validation and Perf Team in coordination with the ABI and Runtime Team and Shared Subsystems Pod as the current gate rollback owners: keep those limits local-only or intentionally promote a broader shared CI perf-coverage claim in `Documentation/zigux/phase4-validation-matrix.md` and `Documentation/zigux/review-checklist.md` without widening the current validator-first packet by accident. Current master already keeps `Documentation/zigux/phase4-validation-matrix.md`, `Documentation/zigux/review-checklist.md`, `Documentation/zigux/README.md`, `scripts/zigux/README.md`, and `scripts/zigux/validate-phase4.py` on the local-only side of that boundary, so the next honest follow-through is the explicit shared-promotion decision itself rather than another reminder-sync pass.
